1.he: קָנִיתִי לִי סְחוֹרָה וּמִקְוֵה. לִמְצֹא בָהּ רֶוַח וּמִקְוֶה
1.note: A rhyme on one word with two senses: מִקְוֵה is "goods" or "stock" (read so in 1 Kgs 10:28), and מִקְוֶה in the next line is "hope" (as in Jer 14:8).

2.note: צִנָּה means both "shield" and "cold" (Prov 25:13 "the cold of snow"). The next lines go on with Ps 91:4 "a shield and buckler" (צִנָּה וְסֹחֵרָה).

3.note: Eccl 2:8, a phrase of uncertain sense; here read, as often in medieval Hebrew, as women or concubines.

4.he: וּפָשַׁטְנוּ רִקְמָה וְתוֹלַעַת. וְלָבַשְׁנוּ רִמָּה וְתוֹלַעַת
4.note: תּוֹלַעַת is both "scarlet" (the dye) and "worm"; רִקְמָה "embroidery" and רִמָּה "maggot" sound alike. The image of maggot and worm as a cover is from Isa 14:11.

5.note: Ps 58:5–6: the deaf adder that does not hear the charmer who casts spells (חוֹבֵר חֲבָרִים). חֲבָרָיו can also mean "his companions", and it plays on the name of Ḥever (חֶבֶר), whose words the people do not hear.

6.note: Literally "and his liver" (כָּבֵד), a seat of feeling (Lam 2:11). "Toward him" is probably the father; the sense is uncertain.
